subject: Prior for covariance between latent variables

messages.author: 495d67130a446b65
messages.subject: Prior for covariance between latent variables
parts:
Hello.

I am trying to fit a structural model with a covariance between two factors. I am using the default beta(1,1) prior for rho. 

I think that the rho prior distribution should look like hist(rbeta(1e6, 1, 1)), but when I run

fit <- bsem(model, data = data, prisamp = T)
plot(fit, plot.type = "hist", pars = 41) # paramater 41 is a covariance between two factors

I obtain a plot similar to hist(rbeta(1e6, 0.3, 0.3)).

I apologize if this a misunderstanding of how probability distributions work, but I think that the plot of the prior samples imply that correlations extremely negative and extremely positive are more probable than any other values.

Is there a way in blavaan to set a prior such that positive correlations are much more likely than extremely negative or near zero correlations?

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Prior for covariance between latent variables
parts:
Could you send the code for the full model? This is possibly a case of "opaque" priors related to the recent paper that I posted here:

https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08667

See the "positive definite constraints" section. But the U-shaped distribution that you describe is unexpected; it is usually the reverse.

For specifying that positive correlations are more likely, the first beta parameter should be larger than the second. For example, beta(30,20) might be fairly reasonable:

-1 + 2 * rbeta(1e6, 30, 20)

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Prior for covariance between latent variables
parts:
Thanks for the code. I found a bug where, for your model, the posterior distribution is still estimated even though prisamp = TRUE. To work around it, add

meanstructure = TRUE

to your bsem command. The bug is also fixed on github.

Also, the warning about "the actual prior might differ from the stated prior" does not apply to your model. You could safely use any beta prior for the single free correlation. If you wanted something other than beta(30, 20), I would recommend to look at various histograms of random numbers from beta distributions, e.g.,

hist(-1 + 2 * rbeta(1e5, 40, 25))

until you find some suitable beta parameters.

Ed
